John Beal

Bassist John Beal is the very definition of a versatile working musician. He has spent seven decades playing onstage and in studios with the likes of Kenny Davern, Harry Belafonte and Leonard Bernstein.
John was interviewed via Zoom on June 18, 2024 by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.
My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m very pleased to have bassist John Beal with me today. Welcome, sir.
Thanks, Monk.
Congratulations on your lengthy career. I assume you know a fellow named John Wasserman?
Where would I know John Wasserman?
Well because he’s a bass player I think, but he wrote this column on the 50 greatest bass players.
Oh yeah, Ron, sure.

Well, and then he did some math. I don’t know if you’ve seen this and I don’t know what year this was, but he did some math and he took in account your work with the American Symphony and studio work and Broadway shows etcetera etcetera, and he came up with oh gosh, close to 30,000 gigs for John Beal.
Wow, doesn’t he have anything better to do? You know? You can spend the time practicing, that would be good. No, he’s the principal bass in the New York City Ballet.
Okay.

I happened to work with his father who was a drummer, one of my first club dates in New York, like a wedding or something. And then I met Ron later at a Wall-to-Wall Bach program at Symphony Space. He sat in with the orchestra. I think he was about 17 or something. So I’ve known him for a while, but I haven’t seen him for a while.

Well when I was looking at your resumes etcetera, this thought came into my head that if you haven’t written a book, you should, and I have the title. Are you ready? It goes something like this (it might have to be edited): John Beal, bassist, Baroque to Bach to Bop to Bernstein to Big Band to Broadway, to Big Bird and Belafonte. I couldn’t fit in Philip Glass, it didn’t have the right ring to it.
That’s too long a title. You need a two-word title.
Well if you had to put it into one word, could you put your career into one or two words?
Better than working. Better than working for a living.
